subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
subtype: Stage 1: The news and the glow [Actor]
passage:
Subject: guess who's team lead 😊

Yash!
I had to tell you before the family group chat explodes. At 4 p.m. today my manager called me into the small meeting room and said they want me to lead the payments team from the first of next month. Me. The girl who cried over her first code review.
Five years, Yash. All those late deployments, all those weekends fixing things nobody noticed. Somebody noticed.
I called Papa from the parking lot and he didn't say anything for a few seconds, then he said, 'I'm going to tell Chachaji first.' Ma has already sent sweets to the neighbours, I'm sure. My old team took me for kulfi and Deepa made a card with a crown on it.
I keep grinning at nothing on the metro. I feel like it's been earned. Is that allowed?
Call me this weekend.
Rashmi

qa.q: When does Rashmi start leading the payments team?
qa.a: From the first of next month.

qa.q: How does Rashmi feel about the promotion, and what shows it?
qa.a: She feels proud and validated, grinning at nothing on the metro and saying it feels earned.

qa.q: What could Rashmi do to enjoy this moment and stay grounded as she starts?
qa.a: She could celebrate with the people who helped her, and keep asking her old team for honest feedback once she starts leading them.

qa.q: How might Rashmi's Papa be feeling when he goes silent for a few seconds?
qa.a: He may be overwhelmed with pride and emotion, and eager to share his daughter's news with the family.

grounding: It shows a well-liked engineer made team lead feeling proud and validated after years of effort, with family and friends celebrating.

subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
subtype: Stage 1: The news and the glow [Actor]
passage:
Sunaina, sit, sit, I have to tell you properly. So at the end of the quarterly meeting, my director says, 'One more thing. From next month, Nandini will be leading the mobile team. She's earned it.' Just like that, in front of everyone. And the whole room clapped. Even Arvind, who I thought didn't like me.
I went to the washroom and just looked at myself in the mirror. Six years. You remember my first job? The one where I was fixing printers?
And then my phone went mad. My mother cried on the call, Sunaina. My brother sent twenty messages in capitals. Your mother even messaged me! How did she know so fast?
I know it's just a title. But it doesn't feel like just a title. It feels like someone finally looked at all those years and said yes, we saw.
Okay, stop smiling at me. Order the samosas, I'm paying.

qa.q: Who clapped when the director made the announcement?
qa.a: The whole room clapped, even Arvind.

qa.q: What does Nandini mean when she says 'It feels like someone finally looked at all those years'?
qa.a: She feels her long effort has been seen and rewarded, and that the promotion validates her.

qa.q: What small habit could help Nandini carry this pride well into the new role?
qa.a: She could keep meeting old friends like Sunaina and colleagues like Arvind the same way, so the glow doesn't change how she treats people.

qa.q: What is it like for Sunaina to hear the news in person?
qa.a: Sunaina gets to share a friend's joy up close and is clearly happy for Nandini, since Nandini tells her to stop smiling.

grounding: It shows an engineer promoted to lead feeling proud and validated after years of effort, with family and friends congratulating her.
